nodes.title: Chat input
nodes.blurb: The user's message enters here.
nodes.explain: Every app has exactly one entry point. It receives the user's message and starts the loop.

fields.label: Greeting shown in the chat UI

nodes.title: Reply
nodes.blurb: Send the final answer back.
nodes.explain: Ends the turn and streams the last message to the user. Any branch that stops without a Reply ends here implicitly.

nodes.title: Agent
nodes.blurb: A model with a job and tools.
nodes.explain: Runs a tool-calling loop: think, call a tool, read the result, repeat, answer. Attach tools, knowledge or memory underneath it.
nodes.tradeoff: More tools give more reach but more chances to pick the wrong one. Keep each agent focused.

fields.label: Job in one line
fields.help: Shown to supervisors so they know when to delegate here.

fields.label: Model
fields.help: Leave on default to use the project model.

fields.label: Reasoning effort
fields.help: Claude only. Higher effort thinks longer and costs more. Low suits routing and chat.

fields.label: Temperature
fields.help: Only sent to models that accept it. Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable ignore it; use effort instead.

nodes.title: Supervisor
nodes.blurb: Delegates to worker agents.
nodes.explain: Reads the conversation, picks the next worker, and repeats until the job is done. Workers you connect from 'Delegate' report back automatically.
nodes.tradeoff: Flexible and good at open-ended tasks, but every round costs a model call. Cap the rounds.

fields.label: Model
fields.help: Leave on default to use the project model.

nodes.title: LLM step
nodes.blurb: One model call, no tools.
nodes.explain: A single, predictable model call: summarise, rewrite, translate, extract. Cheaper and faster than an agent.

fields.label: Model
fields.help: Leave on default to use the project model.

fields.label: Temperature
fields.help: Only sent to models that accept it. Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable ignore it; use effort instead.

nodes.title: Router
nodes.blurb: Send each request down one branch.
nodes.explain: Classifies the latest message and follows the matching branch. Use a model for nuance, or keywords for zero cost.
nodes.tradeoff: Model routing handles fuzzy requests; keyword routing is free, instant and predictable.

fields.label: Model
fields.help: Leave on default to use the project model.

nodes.title: Review loop
nodes.blurb: Check the answer, send it back if weak.
nodes.explain: A reviewer model grades the latest answer against your criteria. 'Revise' loops back with feedback; 'Pass' moves on. The loop stops after the max attempts.
nodes.tradeoff: Raises quality noticeably, at the cost of one extra call per attempt.

fields.label: Model
fields.help: Leave on default to use the project model.

nodes.title: Custom step
nodes.blurb: Your own Python, described in words.
nodes.explain: Anything the toolkit lacks. Describe it and Claude writes the function, or write it yourself. It lands in backend/app/custom/nodes.py.

nodes.title: Knowledge base
nodes.blurb: Your documents, indexed for search.
nodes.explain: Loads, chunks and embeds your files into a vector store. Attach it under an agent (as a search tool) or into a Retrieve step.
nodes.tradeoff: Hybrid search finds exact terms that pure vector search misses. A reranker improves precision but adds latency.

fields.label: What's inside
fields.help: Agents read this to decide when to search.

options.label: pgvector (Postgres)
options.hint: One database for vectors, chat history and app data.

options.label: Local (BGE small)
options.hint: Runs on CPU via fastembed. No API key.

nodes.title: Retrieve step
nodes.blurb: Always look things up before answering.
nodes.explain: Searches the attached knowledge base with the latest message and hands the results to the next step. Classic RAG: predictable, one search per turn.
nodes.tradeoff: Always searches, even when not needed. Attaching knowledge to an agent instead lets the agent decide.

nodes.title: Web search
nodes.blurb: Search the live web (Tavily).
nodes.explain: Returns titles, links and snippets for a query. Needs TAVILY_API_KEY.

nodes.title: Read web page
nodes.blurb: Fetch a URL as clean text.
nodes.explain: Downloads a page and strips it to readable text. Pairs well with web search.

nodes.title: HTTP API
nodes.blurb: Call one endpoint of your API.
nodes.explain: Turns a single REST endpoint into a tool. Parameters become tool inputs the model fills in.

fields.label: When should the agent call it?

nodes.title: MCP server
nodes.blurb: Every tool from an MCP server.
nodes.explain: Connects to a Model Context Protocol server and exposes all of its tools to the agent. Works with local (stdio) and remote (HTTP) servers.

nodes.title: Calculator
nodes.blurb: Exact arithmetic.
nodes.explain: Safely evaluates maths expressions so the model never guesses at numbers.

nodes.title: SQL database
nodes.blurb: Query your database.
nodes.explain: Gives the agent a list-tables tool, a describe-table tool and a read-only query tool.
nodes.tradeoff: Keep read-only on unless you really need writes. Pair writes with a human approval step.

nodes.title: Custom tool
nodes.blurb: Describe a tool; Claude writes it.
nodes.explain: For anything without a ready-made block. Describe the tool and its inputs, and Claude writes typed Python that passes a contract test. The code is saved into your spec, so exports stay repeatable.

nodes.title: Memory
nodes.blurb: Conversation history and long-term facts.
nodes.explain: Short-term memory keeps each conversation thread (and is what lets approvals pause and resume). Long-term memory gives attached agents remember and recall tools that persist across threads.
nodes.tradeoff: Postgres survives restarts and scales; SQLite is a single file; in-memory resets on restart.

nodes.title: Guardrail
nodes.blurb: Screen messages before they go further.
nodes.explain: Deterministic checks, no model call: redact emails, phone and card numbers, block common prompt-injection phrases, cap length, block terms.

nodes.title: Human approval
nodes.blurb: Pause until a person signs off.
nodes.explain: Pauses the run and shows an approval card in the chat UI. The run resumes exactly where it stopped, even after a restart if memory is persistent.

anthropic.label: Claude Opus 5.5

anthropic.label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
anthropic.hint: Faster and cheaper. Good for high-volume workers.

anthropic.label: Claude Haiku 4.5
anthropic.hint: Fastest and cheapest. Good for routers and critics.

anthropic.label: Claude Fable 5.1
anthropic.hint: Anthropic's most capable model, priced above Opus. For the hardest long tasks.

project_fields.help: Claude only. Default lets the model decide.

project.name: docs-qa
project.description: Answer questions over your company PDFs and Markdown, with sources.

You answer questions about the company's documents.
Always search the knowledge base before answering. Quote the source file for every claim.
If the documents don't contain the answer, say so plainly instead of guessing.

blueprints.title: Support desk

project.description: Triage support requests to billing or technical agents. Refunds need a human sign-off.

data.label: Chat input
data.greeting: Hi! How can we help today?

data.label: Screen message
data.blocked_message: Sorry, I can't help with that request.

data.label: Triage
data.instructions: Pick the route that best matches the latest user message.

routes.label: Technical
routes.description: Bugs, errors, how-to questions about the product

data.label: Billing agent
data.system_prompt: You handle billing questions. Look up the order before discussing it. Offer refunds only when the order qualifies, and explain why.

data.label: Technical agent
data.role: Solves product problems using the help centre.

data.label: Friendly reply

data.label: Approve refund

data.label: Orders API

blueprints.title: Research team
blueprints.blurb: A supervisor delegates to three workers; a reviewer loops until the report holds up.

project.name: research-team
project.description: A supervisor runs a researcher, an analyst and a writer, and a reviewer checks the report.

data.label: Research lead
data.instructions:
You lead a small research team. Plan the work, then delegate one step at a time:
- researcher: finds and reads sources on the web
- analyst: checks numbers and does calculations
- writer: drafts the final report
Finish once the writer has produced a report that answers the question.

data.label: Researcher
data.role: Finds and reads sources on the web.
data.system_prompt: Search the web, open the most relevant pages and report key facts with their URLs. Prefer primary sources.

data.label: Analyst
data.system_prompt: Verify every number the team relies on. Use the calculator for arithmetic. Flag anything that doesn't add up.

data.label: Writer
data.system_prompt: Write a clear, well-structured report from the team's findings. Use headings and cite sources inline.

data.label: Fact check
data.criteria: Every claim is supported by a cited source, numbers are consistent, and the report answers the original question.

blueprints.title: Content studio
blueprints.blurb: Writer and editor loop, then human sign-off before publishing.

project.name: content-studio
project.description: Draft, self-review in a loop, then a human approves before publishing.

data.label: Writer
data.system_prompt: Write the requested piece. Match the brand voice: plain, warm, specific. When you receive reviewer feedback, revise the whole draft.

data.label: Editor review
data.criteria: Clear structure, no filler, a concrete call to action, under the requested length, no factual claims without support.

blueprints.title: SQL analyst
blueprints.blurb: Plain-English questions over your database, read-only, explained simply.

project.name: data-analyst
project.description: Ask questions about your database in plain English. Read-only by default.

data.label: Chat input

data.label: Screen message

data.label: SQL analyst
data.role: Answers questions by querying the database.
data.system_prompt: Explore the schema first, then write one careful SQL query. Show the query you ran. Never guess column names.

data.label: Explain simply
data.instructions: Rewrite the analyst's findings for a non-technical reader: the answer first, then two lines of context.
